title: HLA-B*57:01 Screening to Prevent Abacavir Hypersensitivity (PREDICT-1)
text_chunk: Mallal et al. (NEJM, 2008) conducted PREDICT-1, a prospective, randomized, double-blind study of 1956 HIV-infected patients from 265 centers in 19 countries. Patients were randomized to prospective HLA-B*57:01 screening (with exclusion of carriers from abacavir) vs standard of care. Immunologically confirmed abacavir HSR occurred in 0% of the screening arm vs 2.7% of controls (p<0.001). Clinically suspected HSR was 3.4% vs 7.8%. The study established that HLA-B*57:01 screening eliminates immunologically confirmed abacavir hypersensitivity with 100% negative predictive value, providing the definitive evidence for universal pre-treatment screening.
outcome_measure: Immunologically confirmed hypersensitivity reaction rate
outcome_value: 0% in screening arm vs 2.7% in control (p<0.001)

title: Genotype-Guided Warfarin Dosing vs Standard Dosing (EU-PACT)
text_chunk: Pirmohamed et al. (NEJM, 2013) conducted EU-PACT, a single-blind RCT of 455 patients starting warfarin across 3 European countries. Patients were randomized to genotype-guided dosing (CYP2C9+VKORC1 algorithm) vs standard clinical dosing. The primary outcome, percentage of time in therapeutic INR range (TTR) during weeks 4-12, was significantly higher in the genotype-guided arm (67.4% vs 60.3%, p<0.001). Genotype-guided patients also had fewer INR values >=4.0 (27% vs 37%, p=0.03) and shorter time to stable dose. This was the first large RCT to demonstrate clinical superiority of PGx-guided warfarin dosing.
outcome_measure: Time in therapeutic INR range (TTR), weeks 4-12
outcome_value: 67.4% PGx-guided vs 60.3% control (p<0.001)

title: Genotype-Guided vs Clinically-Guided Warfarin Dosing (COAG)
text_chunk: Kimmel et al. (NEJM, 2013) conducted COAG, a multicenter, double-blind RCT of 1015 patients initiating warfarin at 18 US clinical centers. Patients were randomized to genotype-guided (CYP2C9+VKORC1 algorithm) vs clinical algorithm-guided dosing. The primary outcome, TTR during the first 4 weeks, was not significantly different between groups (45.2% vs 45.4%, p=0.91). However, subgroup analysis revealed that in African American patients, the genotype-guided algorithm performed worse, possibly due to untyped CYP2C9 alleles (*5, *6, *8, *11) prevalent in this population. COAG highlighted the importance of comprehensive genotyping panels inclusive of population-specific variants.
outcome_measure: Time in therapeutic INR range (TTR), first 4 weeks
outcome_value: 45.2% PGx-guided vs 45.4% control (p=0.91, NS)

title: Pre-emptive Pharmacogenomic Testing for Preventing Adverse Drug Reactions (PREPARE/U-PGx)
text_chunk: Swen et al. (Lancet, 2023) reported the PREPARE study, the largest prospective PGx implementation trial. 6944 patients across 7 European countries were randomized to pre-emptive genotyping of a 12-gene panel vs standard of care. The study used a genotype-guided prescribing card with DPWG/CPIC recommendations. The primary endpoint — clinically relevant adverse drug reactions within 12 weeks — was significantly reduced in the PGx group (21.0% vs 27.7%, absolute risk reduction 6.7%, RR 0.79, p=0.0006). This demonstrated that pre-emptive multi-gene pharmacogenomic testing reduces adverse drug reactions across multiple drug-gene pairs in routine clinical practice.
gene: 12-gene panel (CYP2D6, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, CYP3A5, CYP2B6, DPYD, TPMT, NUDT15, UGT1A1, SLCO1B1, VKORC1, HLA-B)
outcome_measure: Clinically relevant adverse drug reactions within 12 weeks

title: SLCO1B1 Variants and Statin-Induced Myopathy (SEARCH Collaborative Group)
text_chunk: The SEARCH Collaborative Group (NEJM, 2008) conducted a genome-wide association study in 85 patients with definite or incipient myopathy during simvastatin 80mg treatment vs 90 controls. A single strong GWAS signal at SLCO1B1 (rs4149056, c.521T>C) explained 60% of myopathy cases. The C allele conferred odds ratio 4.5 per allele (p=2x10^-9). CC homozygotes had 16.9-fold increased myopathy risk. This landmark GWAS study identified the first genome-wide significant pharmacogenomic variant and led to FDA label changes for simvastatin, the 80mg dose restriction, and CPIC statin guidelines.
outcome_measure: Simvastatin-induced myopathy risk (OR)
outcome_value: OR 4.5 per C allele; OR 16.9 for CC homozygotes (p=2x10^-9)

title: DPYD-Guided Dose Individualization of Fluoropyrimidine Therapy (Dutch prospective study)
text_chunk: Henricks et al. (Lancet Oncol, 2018) reported a prospective, multicenter study of 1103 patients receiving fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy with upfront DPYD genotyping. Patients with DPYD variants received genotype-guided dose reductions per DPWG guidelines. Among 85 DPD-deficient patients (7.7%), genotype-guided dosing reduced grade >=3 fluoropyrimidine toxicity from the historical rate of 73% to 28% (p<0.001). Overall treatment-related mortality in DPD-deficient patients dropped from 10% to 0%. Non-DPD-deficient patients maintained standard efficacy. Cost-effectiveness analysis showed testing cost of ~150 EUR per patient was vastly outweighed by savings from prevented hospitalization for severe toxicity.
outcome_measure: Grade >=3 fluoropyrimidine toxicity in DPD-deficient patients
outcome_value: 28% genotype-guided vs 73% historical (p<0.001); 0% vs 10% treatment-related mortality

title: Genotype-Guided Oral P2Y12 Inhibitor Selection After PCI (TAILOR-PCI)
text_chunk: Pereira et al. (JAMA, 2020) reported the TAILOR-PCI trial, a prospective, open-label RCT of 5302 patients undergoing PCI. CYP2C19 loss-of-function carriers were randomized to ticagrelor vs clopidogrel; non-carriers received clopidogrel. The primary endpoint (cardiovascular death, MI, stroke, stent thrombosis, severe recurrent ischemia at 12 months) was reduced in the genotype-guided arm among LOF carriers (4.0% vs 5.9%), though the primary intention-to-treat analysis was not statistically significant (HR 0.66, p=0.06). However, the pre-specified per-protocol analysis was significant (HR 0.21, p=0.01). The trial supported CYP2C19-guided antiplatelet selection and informed subsequent clinical adoption.
outcome_measure: MACE at 12 months in CYP2C19 LOF carriers
outcome_value: 4.0% ticagrelor vs 5.9% clopidogrel (HR 0.66, p=0.06 ITT; HR 0.21, p=0.01 per-protocol)

title: CYP2C19 Genotype-Guided Antiplatelet De-escalation (POPular Genetics)
text_chunk: Claassens et al. (NEJM, 2019) reported the POPular Genetics trial, a randomized, open-label, assessor-blinded, non-inferiority trial of 2488 patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI in the Netherlands. Patients in the genotype-guided arm received clopidogrel if CYP2C19 *1/*1 or *1/*17 (72%) and ticagrelor/prasugrel if carrying LOF alleles (28%). The genotype-guided strategy was non-inferior to standard ticagrelor/prasugrel for net adverse clinical events (5.1% vs 5.9%, HR 0.87) while significantly reducing bleeding (9.8% vs 12.5%, HR 0.78, p=0.04). This trial validated genotype-guided de-escalation from potent P2Y12 inhibitors to clopidogrel in appropriate patients.
outcome_measure: Net adverse clinical events and bleeding at 12 months
outcome_value: NACE 5.1% vs 5.9% (non-inferior); bleeding 9.8% vs 12.5% (p=0.04, superior)

title: Indiana University Genomic Medicine Implementation (INFORM PGx)
text_chunk: Pratt et al. (Clin Pharmacol Ther, 2020) described the INFORM PGx study at Indiana University, which implemented pre-emptive pharmacogenomic testing for 6000 patients using a 27-gene panel. Within 12 months, 28% of patients had an actionable drug-gene interaction identified. CYP2D6 had the highest proportion of actionable findings (35% of patients carried variant alleles), followed by CYP2C19 (30%) and SLCO1B1 (25%). The study demonstrated feasibility of health-system-wide pre-emptive PGx testing with automated CDS alerts in the EHR. Provider acceptance was 72% for CDS recommendations.
outcome_measure: Actionable drug-gene interactions identified; provider acceptance rate
outcome_value: 28% of patients had actionable findings; 72% provider acceptance of CDS alerts

title: Mayo Clinic RIGHT Protocol — Pre-emptive PGx Testing in Primary Care
text_chunk: Bielinski et al. (Clin Pharmacol Ther, 2014) and subsequent publications described the RIGHT (Right Drug, Right Dose, Right Time) study at Mayo Clinic, which implemented pre-emptive pharmacogenomic testing using a custom PGx array in >10,000 patients. The program identified that 99% of patients carry at least one actionable pharmacogenomic variant. Integration with the Epic EHR provided real-time CDS alerts at point-of-prescribing. The RIGHT 10K study demonstrated that pre-emptive testing is operationally feasible in a large health system and that most patients have PGx results available before their first actionable prescription.
gene: CYP2D6, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, SLCO1B1, VKORC1, DPYD, TPMT, CYP3A5
outcome_measure: Prevalence of actionable PGx variants; feasibility of EHR integration
outcome_value: 99% of patients carry at least one actionable PGx variant

title: Electronic Medical Records and Genomics (eMERGE-PGx) Network Implementation
text_chunk: Rasmussen-Torvik et al. (Pharmacogenomics, 2014) and subsequent publications described the eMERGE-PGx Network, which implemented PGx testing across 9 eMERGE network sites including Vanderbilt, Geisinger, Northwestern, Cincinnati Children's, and others. The network genotyped >25,000 patients using the PGx-seq platform covering 84 pharmacogenes. Key findings: 96.2% of participants carried at least one actionable PGx variant (CPIC Level A/B). The most common actionable findings were CYP2C19 IM/PM (27%), CYP2D6 IM/PM (25%), and SLCO1B1 decreased function (20%). The network established best practices for PGx result return, EHR integration, and clinical decision support.
outcome_measure: Prevalence of actionable PGx variants across 9 sites
outcome_value: 96.2% carry at least one actionable variant; CYP2C19 IM/PM 27%, CYP2D6 IM/PM 25%

title: CYP3A5 Genotype-Based Tacrolimus Dosing in Kidney Transplantation (TACTICS)
text_chunk: Thervet et al. (Lancet, 2010) conducted a randomized controlled trial of 280 de novo kidney transplant recipients comparing CYP3A5 genotype-adapted tacrolimus dosing vs body weight-based standard dosing. CYP3A5 expressers in the genotype arm received 0.30 mg/kg/day (vs 0.20 mg/kg/day standard). The primary endpoint, proportion achieving target tacrolimus trough (10-15 ng/mL) on day 3, was significantly higher in the genotype arm (43.2% vs 29.1%, p=0.03). Genotype-guided dosing allowed faster achievement of therapeutic drug levels without increased toxicity or rejection.
outcome_measure: Proportion achieving target trough on day 3 post-transplant
outcome_value: 43.2% genotype-guided vs 29.1% standard (p=0.03)

title: Paroxetine Co-Prescription and Breast Cancer Mortality During Tamoxifen Therapy
text_chunk: Kelly et al. (BMJ, 2010) conducted a population-based cohort study of 2430 women aged >=66 years receiving adjuvant tamoxifen for breast cancer, examining the impact of concurrent CYP2D6 inhibitor (paroxetine) use on mortality. Overlap of paroxifen and tamoxifen for >=25% of the tamoxifen treatment period was associated with a significant increase in breast cancer mortality (adjusted HR 1.91, 95% CI 1.35-2.69). Other SSRIs (sertraline, citalopram, fluvoxamine) that are weaker CYP2D6 inhibitors were not associated with increased mortality. This study provided critical real-world evidence for phenoconversion affecting tamoxifen efficacy.
outcome_measure: Breast cancer-specific mortality
outcome_value: HR 1.91 (95% CI 1.35-2.69) for paroxetine co-prescription >=25% overlap

title: Genotype-Informed Warfarin Dosing in Orthopedic Patients (GIFT)
text_chunk: Gage et al. (JAMA, 2017) conducted GIFT, a pragmatic, randomized clinical trial of 1650 older adults initiating warfarin after elective hip or knee arthroplasty. Patients were randomized to genotype-guided dosing (CYP2C9+VKORC1+CYP4F2 algorithm) vs clinically-guided dosing. The primary composite endpoint (major bleeding, INR >=4, VTE, death within 30 days) was significantly lower in the genotype-guided arm (10.8% vs 14.7%, RR 0.73, p=0.02). This was the first US-based warfarin RCT to show clinical benefit of PGx-guided dosing, complementing the European EU-PACT results.
outcome_measure: Composite: major bleeding, INR>=4, VTE, death at 30 days
outcome_value: 10.8% PGx-guided vs 14.7% control (RR 0.73, p=0.02)

title: Discovery of HLA-B*15:02 and Carbamazepine-Induced SJS/TEN
text_chunk: Chung et al. (Nature, 2004) conducted a case-control study comparing HLA alleles in 44 Han Chinese patients with carbamazepine-induced SJS/TEN vs 101 carbamazepine-tolerant controls and 93 healthy controls. HLA-B*15:02 was present in 100% (44/44) of SJS/TEN cases vs 3% of tolerant controls (OR >2500, p=3.13x10^-27). This was the first identification of an HLA allele as a pharmacogenomic biomarker for drug hypersensitivity and established the paradigm for HLA-mediated immune-related adverse drug reactions. The finding led to FDA labeling changes and mandatory HLA-B*15:02 testing in patients of Asian ancestry.
outcome_measure: HLA-B*15:02 frequency in SJS/TEN cases vs controls
outcome_value: 100% in cases vs 3% in controls (OR >2500, p=3.13x10^-27)

title: Implementing GeNomics In pracTicE (IGNITE) Network Outcomes
text_chunk: The IGNITE Network (Cavallari et al., Genet Med 2017; multiple subsequent publications) was an NHGRI-funded network of 6 US sites implementing genomic medicine. Key PGx results included: Vanderbilt PREDICT program showed that pre-emptive genotyping of >35,000 patients reduced adverse cardiovascular events in CYP2C19 LOF clopidogrel users by 60% through genotype-guided alternative antiplatelet selection. Indiana University demonstrated that CYP2C19-guided prescribing was associated with significantly fewer adverse cardiac events (1.3% vs 4.5%, p=0.02). The network provided multi-site evidence that PGx implementation improves clinical outcomes in real-world settings.
outcome_measure: Adverse cardiovascular events with PGx-guided therapy
outcome_value: 60% reduction in adverse cardiovascular events with CYP2C19-guided clopidogrel at Vanderbilt

title: Worldwide Prevalence of Actionable Pharmacogenomic Variants (1000 Genomes Analysis)
text_chunk: Chanfreau-Coffinier et al. (Clin Pharmacol Ther, 2019) analyzed data from the 1000 Genomes Project and gnomAD to determine the global prevalence of actionable pharmacogenomic variants across 26 populations. Key findings: >99% of individuals carry at least one actionable PGx variant. CYP2D6 IM/PM phenotype prevalence: 30-40% globally. CYP2C19 IM/PM: 20-35% European, 40-65% East Asian. SLCO1B1 c.521 TC/CC: 15-30% European. The study demonstrated that pharmacogenomic variation is universal and that PGx testing has high clinical yield regardless of patient ancestry.
outcome_measure: Prevalence of actionable PGx variants by population
outcome_value: >99% of individuals carry at least one actionable PGx variant globally

title: TPMT Genotype-Guided Thiopurine Dosing in Childhood ALL (St. Jude Total Therapy)
text_chunk: Relling et al. (multiple St. Jude Total Therapy publications, 1999-2019) established the paradigm for TPMT-guided mercaptopurine dosing in pediatric ALL. In prospective implementation across Total Therapy XIII-XVI protocols (>1500 patients), TPMT genotyping at diagnosis with preemptive dose reduction for heterozygotes (50%) and homozygous variants (90%) virtually eliminated thiopurine-related hospitalization for myelosuppression in TPMT-variant patients while maintaining leukemia-free survival. Subsequently, addition of NUDT15 genotyping further refined dosing, particularly for East Asian patients. This represents the longest-running and most comprehensively validated PGx implementation program.
study_type: Prospective implementation across multiple clinical trials
outcome_measure: Thiopurine-related myelosuppression hospitalization
outcome_value: Near-elimination of myelosuppression hospitalization in TPMT-variant patients; maintained leukemia-free survival

title: Reduced-Dose Efavirenz Non-Inferiority (ENCORE1)
text_chunk: ENCORE1 Study Group (Lancet, 2014) conducted a double-blind, randomized, non-inferiority trial comparing efavirenz 400mg vs 600mg (standard dose) in 630 treatment-naive HIV-infected patients across 38 sites globally. The primary endpoint, virological suppression (HIV-1 RNA <200 copies/mL) at 48 weeks, was non-inferior for 400mg (90.0% vs 89.5%, difference 0.5%, 95% CI -5.3 to 6.2). The 400mg dose had fewer CNS adverse events. This trial provided evidence supporting CYP2B6 genotype-guided dose reduction, as CYP2B6 slow metabolizers on 600mg have equivalent exposure to extensive metabolizers on 400mg.
outcome_measure: Virological suppression at 48 weeks
outcome_value: 90.0% at 400mg vs 89.5% at 600mg (non-inferior)

title: National HLA-B*58:01 Screening Implementation in Taiwan
text_chunk: Ko et al. (JAMA Intern Med, 2015) evaluated the impact of the nationwide HLA-B*58:01 screening program in Taiwan, implemented in 2010. Analysis of national health insurance data showed that allopurinol-associated SJS/TEN incidence decreased from 0.79 per 100,000 person-years (2005-2009) to 0.16 per 100,000 person-years (2011-2014), a >80% reduction (IRR 0.20, 95% CI 0.07-0.59). The screening program was cost-effective, with incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of $2,700 per QALY in the Taiwanese population (HLA-B*58:01 prevalence ~8%). This represents the most successful nationwide PGx screening implementation program globally.
outcome_measure: Allopurinol-associated SJS/TEN incidence rate
outcome_value: 0.16 vs 0.79 per 100,000 person-years (IRR 0.20, >80% reduction)
